source.title: Detecting and Refurbishing Ground Truth Errors During Training of Deep Learning-Based Echocardiography Segmentation Models
source.authors: Iman Islam; B. Ruijsink; Andrew J. Reader; Andrew P. King

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; figure results are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of synthetic training-label errors on segmentation performance, using test Dice rather than the original sources’ random-label experiment. Its random annotation errors do not assign completely random labels to the training set.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for synthetic random and systematic annotation errors, not completely random relabeling. Training error and chance test error are not reported. Figure-only results have no recoverable numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study measures robustness to realistic segmentation annotation errors and evaluates error detection and repair. Its random errors alter selected structures through incomplete annotation, boundary distortion, or merging; they do not randomize target labels independently of image content. Test Dice under these perturbations does not establish random-label fitting or the memorization behavior named in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the discussion: the baseline U-Net was robust to random annotation errors, while refurbishment offered some improvement for systematic errors, especially at moderate corruption levels. These conclusions concern annotation-error robustness, not demonstrated fitting of random labels.
record.recipe_differences: Trains a U-Net on echocardiography segmentation with synthetic annotation errors, then evaluates test Dice; it does not use completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Error type (random versus systematic), error level, and whether the refurbishment pipeline is used affect reported segmentation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3 reports gradually declining test segmentation performance as annotation errors increase, with relatively strong baseline U-Net performance under random errors and greater degradation under systematic errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A U-Net can retain substantial segmentation accuracy despite realistic annotation perturbations that preserve some target structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Experiments 1–3 evaluate identification of corrupted annotations, improvement of annotations through refurbishment, and downstream segmentation gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient variability can identify erroneous segmentation annotations, and selective pseudo-label refurbishment can improve annotation quality and segmentation performance.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
record.problems: The relevant Experiment 3 outcomes are shown only in figures, without numeric values in the supplied text. Training error and chance-level test error are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: Experiment 3 results for random and systematic ground-truth errors are figure-only, and the text does not provide separable numeric outcomes for each model, error type, or level (Figs. 2–3).

untested.parts: Completely random target labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit alongside steadily worsening test error toward chance under increasing random-label corruption. The annotation perturbations preserve image-related target structure, and training fit and chance performance are not reported.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized. The pipeline's warm-up period does not measure this learning order.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's V4 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. The figure-only Experiment 3 outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not assign completely random labels to the training set or report training error and test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed as corruption increases.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The paper studies test performance under random annotation errors, but does not report whether training error remains perfect or whether test error rises toward chance. Figure-only outcomes are described qualitatively and cannot be extracted as separate numerical rows.
No comparison of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
No measurement of the order in which real and noisy labels are learned.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
